happened: On January 20, 2025, President Trump ordered a 90-day pause on most foreign development aid while each program was reviewed. In September 2025 he set the cap for fiscal year 2026 at 7,500 refugees, the lowest ever, with most slots for white South Africans (Afrikaners). happened: On August 21, 2025, the U.S. and the European Union announced a framework trade agreement. A September 2025 executive order and a notice by the U.S. Trade Representative put its tariff terms into effect.

legal: On February 20, 2026, the Supreme Court ruled that the International Emergency Economic Powers Act does not allow tariffs, which struck down the "reciprocal" tariffs that were part of the leverage behind the deal. The President then imposed a temporary 10% surcharge under Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974.
closeness: Broader than a review: the U.S. renegotiated trade terms with the EU using tariffs.
uncertain: Which EU deal terms still apply after the ruling is not fully clear. A September 2026 notice still listed the European Union among trade partners getting lower tariffs on medicines, suggesting the deal remained in use. Newest source: September 2026.

happened: From late 2025, President Trump pressed for U.S. control of Greenland. In January 2026 he threatened, then dropped, tariffs on European allies over the issue. On September 22, 2026, the U.S., Denmark and Greenland signed a defense agreement in New York that adds to a 1951 treaty, expands U.S. military access, bars non-NATO countries from military bases in Greenland, and sets up screening of investment from outside NATO. It still needs approval by the Danish and Greenlandic parliaments.

key_dates.event: Trump announces tariffs on eight European countries over Greenland, later dropped
Trump says he will not use force and announces a 'framework' with NATO
U.S., Denmark and Greenland sign a security agreement in New York

closeness: The agreement adds some economic ties, such as investment screening, but it is mainly a security deal. The administration's push for control of Greenland goes beyond the chapter's call for closer economic ties.
uncertain: The official text was not found; reports differ on how far the investment rules go, and one analysis says Greenland's own authorities run the screening. Parliamentary approval is pending. Newest source: September 2026.
